title: Gloaming ops handoff — late shift summary
content:
Gloaming Ops Handoff (late shift) — 2026-08-24

Shift window: 19:30 - 03:30 PDT
On-call: Asha Mehta (handoff author)
Relief: Ethan Park (starting 03:30)
Secondary contacts: Lina Torres (infra), Connor Wu (runtime)
Slack: #sre-oncall, thread: s/kv-thrash-aug24-synth

Executive summary:
- Two noteworthy incidents during the window: a KV-cache thrash incident causing 95th+ latency spikes (~21:10 PDT), and a short auth token rotation fallout causing 401s for a small subset of internal test clients (~01:45 PDT). Both mitigations restored customer-facing service quickly; follow-ups and runbook deltas listed below.

Incident 1 — KV cache thrash -> tail latency spikes
- Detection: autoscaling alerts + frontend p95 latency alert at 21:09 PDT (alert rule: infra_api_p95>350ms for 5m).
- Affected surface: inference-hosts in pool "gpu-dedicated-n1" handling long-context requests (seq > 2048).
- Likely trigger: an unusual workload pattern from a single internal partner test hitting large sequence inputs concurrently; caused frequent KV cache evictions and thrash leading to serialization/backpressure inside the runtime.
- Timeline:
  * 21:09 PDT — p95 alert fires.
  * 21:11 PDT — detected increased page faults and cache miss ratio on hosts g-rw-07..g-rw-10 (prom query: sum(kv_cache_miss_total) by (host) spiked x8).
  * 21:15 PDT — temporarily routed traffic away from g-rw-07..g-rw-10 using routing policy tag fallback; rerouted to fallback pool "gpu-burst-2".
  * 21:18 PDT — restarted inference process on g-rw-09 to recover local memory fragmentation; observed immediate drop in local latency.
  * 21:25 PDT — stable after routing + one restart; alerted owners and started incident note.
- Mitigation detail: short-term routing to fallback pool + single-instance restart; increase in caching headroom recommended (see follow-ups).
- Impact: 3–7% error-rate increase for long-context requests for ~15 minutes; no data loss; customers with pinned model variants on affected hosts saw higher latencies.
- Post-incident notes: create a dedicated alert for kv_cache_miss_ratio > 5x baseline and a playbook to change routing policy for long-context heavy traffic.
- Jira: JIRA-SRE-1248 created for postmortem + capacity plan.

Incident 2 — Token rotation caused intermittent 401s for internal test clients
- Detection: internal smoke tests in ci/canary started failing at 01:44 PDT; correlating alert for downstream auth errors (auth_401_rate > 2% for 2m).
- Affected surface: internal test clients and a small set of early-adopter customers who use client-managed credentials.
- Root cause: deployment of credential-rotation job (ops/rotate-creds v2) that pushed a new TTL semantics to a subset of clients; some connectors not updated to accept the shorter TTL.
- Timeline:
  * 01:44 PDT — smoke tests fail; alerted on #sre-oncall.
  * 01:47 PDT — rolled back rotation job to previous version; cleared test failures by 01:53 PDT.
  * 02:05 PDT — infra team patched connector library and notified partner owners.
- Mitigation: immediate rollback + patch; advised partner teams to rotate tokens at next scheduled window with patched connector.
- Jira: JIRA-SRE-1253 tracks the connector patch and followups.

Minor anomalies observed:
- Slightly elevated 500s from model metadata service between 22:55–23:10 PDT — traced to short DB connection pool exhaustion; increased pool and added wait metrics. Ticket CON-9876 to update dashboard.
- One node (g-rw-11) reported degraded NVMe throughput at 00:30 PDT — SRE infra to review hardware telemetry next business day.

Runbook deltas / draft suggestions (short-term additions to handoff/runbook):
- New alert suggestion: kv_cache_miss_ratio > 3x baseline for 3m -> page duty owner + automated routing to fallback pool. Add sample prom query:
  * prom: "sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (pool) / sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) by (pool)"
- Add a procedural step for cache-thrash: identify top 3 hosts by miss rate, drain traffic, restart runtime on highest offender, then monitor for 10m before reintroducing.
- For credential-rotation jobs: add preflight smoke test that simulates connector behavior against canary clients before rollout. Add gating step in deployment pipeline.
- Dashboard widget: per-pool KV hit/miss ratio and top hosts by p95 latency (name: "SRE / KV cache health (per pool)").
- Add runbook snippet for graceful routing: command examples included below.

Helpful commands / quick shell snippets (for oncall):
- List hosts by kv miss (prom proxy): curl -s "http://prom.local/api/v1/query?query=sum%20(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m]))%20by%20(host)" | jq
- Drain host: infractl node drain g-rw-09 --reason "kv-thrash-2026-08-24"
- Restart runtime container: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime-g-rw-09
- Switch route policy: rtr update-route --from-pool gpu-dedicated-n1 --to-pool gpu-burst-2 --tag long-context-temp

Open follow-ups / owners (high priority):
- SRE-1248 (Asha) — full incident postmortem + add KV cache alert and playbook. Due 2026-08-27.
- SRE-1253 (Connor) — coordinate connector patch rollout and confirm partner testing windows. Due 2026-08-26.
- INFRA-667 (Lina) — review g-rw-11 NVMe telemetry and determine need for maintenance or replacement. Due 2026-08-28.
- DASH-304 (Ethan) — add KV cache per-pool dashboard widget and KV miss ratio panels. Due 2026-08-26.

Notes to next shift / actions to watch for:
- Watch for any reappearance of p95 spikes on long-context route; if seen, immediately route to gpu-burst-2 and alert infra.
- Keep an eye on smoke tests for auth 401s; connector patch rollout is starting tomorrow morning 09:00 PDT — expect partner followups.
- NVMe telemetry for g-rw-11: Lina will post findings in CON-9876; if hardware I/O errors continue, escalate to hardware vendor.

Things I did that aren't in tickets yet:
- Added a temporary grafana panel in my personal copy for per-host kv miss ratio (panel id temp-gloaming-01).
- Left a note in the runtime repo (link above to PR) with observed stack traces for g-rw-09 restart.

Lessons learned / quick reflections:
- Long-context traffic is a distinct failure mode; default KV sizing assumptions break under concurrent ultra-long sequences. We should formalize a long-context routing policy and a capacity cushion for pools serving sequence-heavy workloads.
- Small, targeted restarts are an effective short-term remedy for memory fragmentation; we should document safe restart cadence in runbooks so oncall knows limits.

Appendix: raw signals and links (for triage)
- Prom query snapshots posted to thread: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/gloaming-kv-snapshots
- Incident tickets: JIRA-SRE-1248, JIRA-SRE-1253
- Infra PR with notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3421
- Confluence note stub: CON-9876 (runbook updates)

End of handoff — leaving Ethan a short list in #sre-oncall pinned message. If anything degrades before morning, escalate to Lina and Connor as primary.

Quick checklist for relay to next shift:
- [ ] Confirm SRE-1248 postmortem created
- [ ] Confirm DASH-304 dashboard panels live
- [ ] Monitor smoke tests for 401 regressions for next 12h
- [ ] Check NVMe telemetry for g-rw-11 on next maintenance window

— Asha Mehta (oncall)
